title: Echo and Terminal Revisited
premise: Petra Blackwood, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, runs the long supply route between two human worlds that severed contact generations ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Petra discovers the signal originates from the cryoship Meridian, whose sleeping passengers hold the genetic archive both colonies need to survive an approaching ecological collapse — but the ship's failing systems can only wake half of them. As Petra races between worlds to broker a shared rescue, they uncover that each colony's founding myth is a lie built on the other's betrayal, and that loyalty to their own people demands burying the truth forever. In the end, Petra wakes neither half alone but splits the archive itself, forcing both worlds to rebuild together from shared inheritance — and choosing truth over either loyalty.
about_author: Tamsin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital agriculture engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep things alive in places that want everything dead.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: POV Petra. On terraformed world Verdance, Petra tends seed vaults and soil beds for colonists still in cryosleep, establishing their quiet devotion and isolation. The emotional beat is tender loneliness: Petra talks to seeds like children. A routine supply run to sister colony Halcyon Reach looms, and Petra notices the interworld comm array has been dark for years.

chapters.title: Long Route Between Silent Worlds
chapters.summary: POV Petra, aboard hauler Kestrel. The crossing between Verdance and Halcyon Reach takes months; Petra catalogs cargo, rations loneliness, and passes the dead relay buoys that once linked the colonies. Flashbacks reveal Petra's grandmother helped sever communications after 'the Fracture.' The beat is haunted routine — Petra inherits silence without understanding it.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Mid-route, the Kestrel catches a repeating distress signal in Pre-Fracture Standard, a language extinct for two centuries. Petra decodes fragments using grandmother's forbidden linguistic archives: the signal names a ship called Meridian and begs for 'the gardeners.' The beat is electric dread — someone out there speaks the language of the fracture.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: POV Petra, searching family records on Verdance. Petra finds sealed correspondence proving the Fracture wasn't mutual misunderstanding but a deliberate blackout ordered by both colonies' founders. The signal coordinates point outside charted space. The beat is vertigo: Petra's inheritance includes complicity, and answering the signal means betraying it.

chapters.title: Answering
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Against protocol, Petra redirects the Kestrel toward the coordinates and transmits a reply in reconstructed Pre-Fracture Standard. Days later, an automated response confirms: the Meridian, a generation ship launched before the colonies diverged, is dying in orbit around a rogue planetoid. The beat is resolve hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Arrived
chapters.summary: POV Petra docking with the Meridian. Inside: ten thousand sleepers, failing cryopods, and an AI caretaker named Vesper who has been sending distress calls for decades into languages no one alive should know. Vesper mistakes Petra for a descendant of the mission's chief gardener — Petra's own ancestor. The beat is uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: Half a Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Petra with Vesper. The AI reveals the crisis: power failure means only five thousand pods can be sustained. The manifest splits cleanly between colonists destined for Verdance and those for Halcyon Reach — and Vesper requires a living authority from each world to authorize which half wakes. The beat is cold arithmetic against warm lives.

chapters.title: Verdance Will Not Answer
chapters.summary: POV Petra transmitting home. Verdance's ruling Conclave refuses contact, demanding Petra abandon the ship; waking any Meridian colonists would expose the Fracture's true history and topple them. Petra's brother Sefen, a Conclave archivist, secretly warns them to come home or be declared void. The beat is betrayal by one's own soil.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Open Door
chapters.summary: POV Petra at Halcyon Reach, where reception is startlingly warm — too warm. Governor Ilsa Reyes embraces the Meridian discovery publicly, offering full support, while quietly steering Petra toward waking only Halcyon-destined sleepers. The beat is seduction: kindness deployed as strategy, and Petra tempted to accept an easy ally.

chapters.title: Vesper's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV alternating Petra/Vesper logs. Deep in the Meridian's archives, Vesper plays recordings from the original voyage: the founders of both colonies were Meridian crew who abandoned the ship deliberately, stealing its genetic archive and leaving the rest to die slowly. The beat is grief — every sacred origin story on both worlds is a theft.

chapters.title: Sefen's Secret Channel
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Sefen breaks ranks, contacting Petra covertly: he's found matching evidence in Verdance's sealed archives and believes exposure could reform the Conclave rather than destroy it — if Petra brings proof home. But Governor Reyes intercepts the transmission and now knows what Petra carries. The beat is fragile hope with a clock ticking.

chapters.title: Sabotage Aboard the Kestrel
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Saboteurs loyal to Reyes cripple the Kestrel's drive and steal the archive copies, stranding Petra aboard the Meridian with dwindling oxygen and a shipful of sleepers. Vesper begins shutting down peripheral pods to buy time — the first deaths. The beat is helplessness sharpened into fury.

chapters.title: Waking the First Sleeper
chapters.summary: POV Petra. To survive and repair the Kestrel, Petra wakes Dr. Amara Okonkwo, a Meridian engineer and the last fluent speaker of Pre-Fracture Standard, frozen for two hundred years. Amara's disorientation and rage at finding her descendants' worlds at war gives Petra an unexpected ally — and a witness no government can dismiss. The beat is grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Through her eyes, the colonies' divergence becomes tragedy rather than villainy: each side genuinely believed the other had betrayed the Meridian first. Amara and Petra record her testimony as both historical record and diplomatic weapon. The beat is reconciliation at the level of story — truth as something that can be rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Gardeners' Code
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Repairing the Kestrel, Petra discovers their grandmother's hidden legacy: she was a Meridian descendant who became a double agent inside Verdance's Conclave, preserving the truth for someone brave enough to carry it. Petra realizes they were raised for this. The beat is inheritance transformed from burden to calling.

chapters.title: Return to Verdance
chapters.summary: POV Petra and Amara arriving under false registry. Verdance is rationing food; the ecological collapse the Meridian's archive could cure is already visible in failing harvests. Sefen smuggles them toward the Conclave chamber, but Reyes's agents are waiting. The beat is dread — walking into the heart of the lie.

chapters.title: Conclave of Lies
chapters.summary: POV Petra before the Conclave. Petra plays Vesper's recordings and Amara testifies; the chamber fractures between denial, panic, and a young faction hungry for truth. The Conclave orders Petra arrested and the Meridian seized for Verdance alone. Sefen springs them during the chaos. The beat is truth spoken and immediately weaponized by everyone.

chapters.title: Reyes's Gamble
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Halcyon Reach's fleet jumps to claim the Meridian outright, forcing a standoff over the sleeper ship. Reyes offers Petra a final bargain: back Halcyon's version publicly and both worlds get the archive peacefully — under her terms. Petra refuses. The beat is the temptation of the lesser lie, declined.

chapters.title: Five Thousand Names
chapters.summary: POV Petra. With fleets converging and pod failures accelerating, Petra proposes the impossible: split the archive itself, wake colonists in mixed lots bound for both worlds, and let no side inherit a pure bloodline or a clean myth. Vesper calculates it can work — if both governments ratify within seventy-two hours. The beat is desperate audacity.

chapters.title: The Standoff at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV multiple, converging. Verdance and Halcyon warships face each other over the dying ship while Petra, Amara, and Sefen broadcast the full Fracture testimony to both populations simultaneously. Ordinary citizens on both worlds begin demanding ratification. The climax turns on whether truth, delivered plainly, can outrank two centuries of loyalty. The beat is held breath.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Ratification comes at the final hour; the mixed awakening begins, and the first newly-woken colonists — strangers to both worlds, heirs to both — step onto the Kestrel's deck. Reyes concedes rather than fire on sleepers; Verdance's young faction seizes the Conclave. The beat is catharsis: the choice Petra was dreading dissolves into a third answer.

chapters.title: Seeds in Shared Soil
chapters.summary: POV Petra, epilogue. One year later, Meridian survivors plant the first joint settlement between the reconciling colonies, and Petra finally opens the garden meant for the unborn to people who are here. Vesper, retired to caretaker of the new archive, asks Petra what loyalty means now. Petra answers: 'Telling the truth even when your people would rather you didn't.' The beat is quiet, earned hope.
